interface.title: TwistScope
interface.field: 2D materials / electron microscopy (twisted bilayers, moiré superlattices)
interface.stage_of_work: planning experiments by simulation, and analysing diffraction patterns and microscope images
interface.what_it_is_for: Simulate the electron-diffraction and real-space moiré patterns of a twisted 2D bilayer, or measure the twist angle with an uncertainty, and the likely material, from a diffraction pattern or an STM/AFM/TEM image.

data.note: There were no test files, so nothing was uploaded. All images came from the built-in simulator, sent across with 'Measure this pattern' or 'Measure the moiré image', or from the two example buttons in the Measure tab ('STM-like, graphene 8°' and 'Diffraction, MoS₂ 16°'). Both put a note on the image saying noise was added. The page loaded with Graphene/Graphene at 6°, not the MoS₂ 16° start the code notes describe. Every special character shows as garbled text (Å as 'Ã…', ° as 'Â°', subscript 2 as 'â‚‚'), which looks like a character-encoding fault on the page.

features.name: Scale-calibrated material lookup
features.general: Turn a measured spacing into physical units using the user's calibration, and match it against a reference table within a tolerance
features.specific: Scale (1/nm per pixel) or Image width (nm), then Measured lattice constant, Closest match with % off, and a Material label naming the candidates it cannot tell apart (e.g. 'Graphene or hBN'); 'Needs a scale' or 'No match within 3%' when that fails. The result follows the calibration entered, so a wrong width gives a wrong material. The Material dropdown is the material choice for moiré-only images; picking it did not change the label when both lattices were visible
steps: read the lattice constant and closest match
read the candidates in the Material label

screens_never_reached: Measuring from the moiré alone (the Material dropdown is 'used when only the moiré is visible'): every simulated real-space image showed atoms, or failed with 'could not separate two lattices or a moiré', so this path never ran
Measuring an uploaded image: the upload control exists, but there were no test files
A case where Correct image stretch visibly changes the result: no stretched image was available to try it on
not_done: Check how noise, strain or off-centre shift affect the angle: the web app has no noise, strain or shift controls. Noise is added at a fixed level when an image is sent across. The README puts this kind of experiment in the twistsim.py command-line tool, which I could not run from a browser. The stretch-correction checkbox made no difference on an unstretched pattern (screens/006.webp).
Upload a real PNG or JPG micrograph or diffraction pattern: there were no test files.

Check the uncertainty on real-space measurements: on simulated real-space images the reported uncertainty was smaller than the actual error. 16.96° ± 0.19° for a true 16° (screens/019.webp), and 3.13° ± 0.02° for a true 3° (screens/026.webp). I only saw this; I did not investigate it further.

Measure angles below about 2°: at 1.5° (graphene/graphene) and 0.5° (graphene/hBN) the tool reported one layer or could not measure, which matches its stated limit. At 1° the replay got a wrong 2.40° ± 0.15° graded 'Clean measurement' (check/screens/013.webp), so results below 2° can be silently wrong.
Arrow keys did not switch between the Simulate and Measure tabs (screens/034.webp); only clicking works.

open_fixes: A task for uploading your own diffraction pattern or micrograph needs a run with real PNG/JPG test files; the upload control was never used.
Measuring from a moiré-only real-space image, where the Material dropdown and image width supply the lattice, needs an image without atomic resolution; none was produced.
Stretch correction needs testing on a stretched figure, such as one copied from a paper (the README cites 10–27% stretch); it was only tried on an unstretched pattern.
The noise, strain and shift robustness tests exist only in the twistsim.py command-line tool and need a run that can execute it outside the browser.
Why the real-space ± underestimates the actual error, and how often sub-2° patterns are graded Clean while wrong, needs a systematic sweep of known angles.
f9 needs a screenshot citing the upload control and a replay before it can carry a check value.
